Run Reactome pathway enrichment for a single TF module

module_enrich.Rd

Given the hub TFs of a module, extracts their target genes from the TF-gene universe, keeps the 20% most variable targets, and runs Reactome over-representation analysis (ReactomePA::enrichPathway(), human) using all the genes of the expression matrix as the background universe. Gene symbols are converted to Entrez IDs with org.Hs.eg.db; symbols without an Entrez ID are left out (a message gives how many). Pathways with a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value < 0.05 are kept. TF names are matched after make.names() on both sides, so the syntactic names returned by compute.TFs.activity() (e.g. NKX2.1) match the names of the network (NKX2-1).

Usage

module_enrich(counts_norm, module_color, hub_tfs, universe, min_genes = 5)

Arguments

counts_norm

A numeric matrix of normalized expression values (genes x samples), with gene symbols as row names.

module_color

Character. Name of the TF module (color label) to analyze.

hub_tfs

A list as returned by identify_hub_TFs(), where the first element maps module names to vectors of hub TF gene symbols.

universe

A data frame of TF-target interactions with at minimum columns source (TF) and target (gene).

min_genes

Integer. Minimum number of genes to test (20% most variable targets); with fewer, no enrichment is computed and a message is given. Default is 5.

Value

A ReactomePA enrichResult object restricted to pathways with adjusted p-value < 0.05, or NULL if no enrichment is found, if none of the targets is in the row names of counts_norm, or if fewer than min_genes genes would be tested.

Details

The result describes the genes regulated by the hub TFs of the module: any set of TFs has hundreds of targets that carry the pathways those TFs regulate, so random sets of TFs also give enriched pathways. It should be read as what the hub TFs of the module regulate, not as evidence that the module itself is special.
